messages:
mira: Quick proposal — can we build a sandboxed preflight runner for runtime config changes? idea: apply patch to an ephemeral routing layer + KV cache, mirror a tiny slice of production traffic, run for X minutes, and gate the real rollout on telemetry signals. low-risk and catches regressions that unit tests miss.

tom: +1 in principle. how is this different from existing `dry-run`?

mira: Dry-run validates config semantics only. This would actually execute routing decisions, batching, caching logic, etc., against production-like requests (no external side effects). think of it as an infra-level simulation with sampled live requests.

devon: We need three things for this to be useful: simple API, safe sampling/quota controls, and clear telemetry gates. Otherwise ops will ignore it.

mira: Agreed. sketch of a simple API:

```http
POST /v1/configs/preview
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "config_patch": { ... },
  "sample_pct": 0.5,            // percent of traffic to mirror into preview env
  "duration_sec": 600,         // how long to run the preview
  "quota_window_ms": 60000     // cap cost per minute to avoid billing surprises
}
```

tom: Nice. Two UX asks: 1) console should show live preview ID and let you abort. 2) preview runs must be pinned to a read-only preview model variant so nothing mutates customer data.

alesha: Telemetry gate thoughts: compare baseline vs preview for a small set of signals with z-score threshold: error_rate, p95 latency, dropped_connections, token_cost_per_request. If any exceed configured delta -> fail. Also surface sample size.

mira: Yeah — we should surface delta and absolute values. And show a replay of failing requests (redacted).

devon: Quota caps are critical. Preview mirroring still generates tokens and costs. Need per-org preview budget plus per-run max. Also ensure preview traffic never counts against real user quotas (bill to preview_bucket).

sam: Implementation nit: runtime needs a mirror path that copies request and response through the runtime stack but short-circuits external effects (no downstream writes). That means we need a consistent read-only mode in connectors.

ops-bot: NOTE: New preview runs must be logged in audit-stream with run_id and initiator.

tom: Locking: what if two people preview conflicting patches? We should allow concurrent previews but make the console warn of overlapping route changes. A write-lock only for the final apply step (TBD).

mira: Proposed console flow:
- user hits "Preview change" -> calls POST /configs/preview -> creates preview_id
- console shows preview panel with live metrics, failing request examples, and quick abort button
- user can request "promote" which triggers a gated rollout API (canary percent + time window)

CLI example:
```bash
redwoodctl preview --patch my.patch.json --sample 1 --duration 900 
# returns PREVIEW_ID=prv_abc123
redwoodctl preview-status $PREVIEW_ID
redwoodctl preview-promote $PREVIEW_ID --canary 5 --window 3600
```

alesha: For telemetry gates let's add a small evaluation harness:
- use bootstrap bootstrap_ci to compute baseline distribution (last 6 hours)
- compute p-values for each metric, fail if p < 0.01 AND relative change > threshold

devon: Edge cases:
- preview target model may be different from production (quantized vs fp16) -> ensure kernel selection mismatch is surfaced.
- cached prefixes may make preview and prod diverge; make sure prefix-empty warmups are part of the run.

mira: Good call. We'll include a warmup mode that sends synthetic prefix-less traffic at start.

tom: Security: KMS keys for preview logs? previews shouldn't expose raw customer prompts. Redact prompt text and only include hashes + token counts in UI by default. Make raw logs available to authorized SREs via gated access.

sam: Implementation plan idea: reuse existing routing policy layer but add a flag `mirror_mode: preview_id` that forks requests. It should go to a separate runtime shard pool with scaled-down capacity.

ops-bot: SUGGESTION: default preview sample_pct = 0.1% for orgs < trial credits, 1% for power users (configurable).

mira: Next steps:
- devon + sam to prototype preview_endpoint and mirror_mode (ETA 2 wks)
- tom + alesha to draft console mockups and gate thresholds (ETA 1 wk)
- security + legal to sign off on redaction policy (ETA 1 wk)
- product / PM to decide default sample/quotas (mira)

tom: One more: when promoting, the rollout API should allow automatic fallback to previous config if telemetry gate trips during canary. like: `promote --auto-rollback true`.

mira: Yep. add to spec. Also let's add a postmortem hook that automatically records preview telemetry for 7 days for audit (but not full logs unless requested).

alesha: I'll draft a telemetry scoring doc with concrete thresholds and example alerts.

devon: OK — if prototype looks good we can run an internal dogfood week where infra team uses previews for all routing changes.

mira: Thanks everyone. Filing follow-up tickets and will post links here when created. :thumbsup:
